expectation: Membrane or cytoplasm staining on myeloid cells (CD14+ macrophages and monocytes) and some T cells. These would be scattered single cells or clusters in stroma and immune infiltrates, a minority of cells. Tumour cells would be stained only in some cancers.
observed: A: yellow in every tile, punctate cells in some, fibrous stroma-like streaks in others. B/C: a few dim scattered cells. D: an elongated streak, not clearly cells. E: cell-shaped VISTA blobs, some on CD14 cells (white), many beside them.
why: In E, VISTA marks distinct cell-shaped cells, part of them on CD14 cells, but contrast is low in B/C and D and some whole-tissue signal follows stromal texture.
notes: VISTA shows discrete cells, some overlapping CD14 myeloid cells in row E, so the stain looks real. But the typical fields are dim and the brightest spot is a fibrous streak, so the signal is weak.
